reading.body:
Snowflake is primarily a data platform company with $4.7 billion in annual revenue, not an AI company, though it has added AI capabilities to its core infrastructure.

The company's position in the AI stack is as a compute and storage layer for data operations that support machine learning workloads. Snowflake Cortex embeds LLM functions, vector search, and governance into the data cloud itself, meaning AI models operate directly on data where it lives rather than requiring separate movement and infrastructure. Snowflake Arctic, an open-licensed LLM, serves as a reference model optimized for the data cloud environment. This architecture trades off independent AI compute specialization for integration with data engineering pipelines.

For AI scaling specifically, Snowflake's constraint is not whether it provides AI capability but whether consolidating AI inference and data processing in one platform reduces the total power and cooling footprint required to train and run models on large datasets. The data shows the company offers both infrastructure (the cloud platform itself) and software (the embedded AI functions), but does not show compute utilization, power consumption, or how much of Snowflake's $4.7 billion revenue comes from AI versus traditional analytics. Without those figures, the contribution of Snowflake's AI products to the broader compute and power demands of the AI ecosystem remains unclear.

profile_text.body:
Snowflake is a public company founded in 2012 and headquartered in Bozeman, Montana. According to its website, the company provides an AI Data Cloud platform that powers AI, data engineering, applications, and analytics. Snowflake describes its offering as enabling organizations to collaborate, build AI-powered data apps, and unlock data insights within a secure and scalable environment, helping customers innovate faster by ingesting, processing, analyzing, and modeling data. The company also offers Snowflake Postgres, which it describes as bringing the world's most popular database to the AI Data Cloud without requiring complex data pipelines.

Snowflake's AI products include Snowflake Arctic, an enterprise-focused large language model available under Apache 2.0 license that integrates with its data cloud for commercial use, and Snowflake Cortex, which provides native AI capabilities within the data cloud including LLM functions, vector search, and data residency controls managed through Snowflake Horizon governance. The company cites customer examples including Under Armour, which it says uses unified data and conversational AI on Snowflake, and Booking.com, which migrated from Hadoop to modernize its data and AI infrastructure.

As a public company trading under ticker SNOW, Snowflake reported revenue of $4,683,946,000 for the fiscal year ended January 31, 2026, according to its 10-K filing.
